body:
Supplied variables make Fusion repeatedly grow dictionary bucket/entry arrays, including on warm cached operations.

This PR supplies a one-time hint before the first successful/default insertion. On .NET 9+, constant-time JSON property-count metadata bounds the hint by declaration count; at most three declarations skip it. .NET 8 is unchanged. Empty/unknown-only/first-error inputs retain empty storage; defaults may grow past the hint.

### Benchmarks

The custom Release .NET 10.0.12 ARM64 harness calls the real helper, excluding setup/output checks. Default server-GC timing: three launches/variant, fifteen minimum-50-ms intervals/case, medians of launch medians. Separate DATAS=0/four-heap allocation validation: two launches/variant, 1,048-byte controls and strict counter/full-GC checks. Ratios are candidate/baseline.

| Case | Baseline median | Candidate median | Time C/B | Baseline B/op | Candidate B/op | Alloc C/B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2 variables | 268.827 ns | 270.581 ns | 1.007 | 288 | 288 | 1.000 |
| 8 variables | 1.155 µs | 1.091 µs | 0.944 | 1,520 | 712 | 0.468 |
| 32 variables | 5.542 µs | 5.393 µs | 0.973 | 3,488 | 2,144 | 0.615 |
| 256 variables | 108.554 µs | 105.385 µs | 0.971 | 37,880 | 16,096 | 0.425 |
| 32 defaults | 1.509 µs | 1.502 µs | 0.995 | 3,488 | 3,488 | 1.000 |
| Sparse 1/32 | 988.938 ns | 929.552 ns | 0.940 | 264 | 264 | 1.000 |
| 1/32 + extra keys | 2.849 µs | 2.807 µs | 0.985 | 264 | 1,760 | 6.667 |
| 1/32 + duplicate used key | 2.925 µs | 2.905 µs | 0.993 | 264 | 1,760 | 6.667 |


Tested candidate `627f45ef85` has identical production blobs to this clean branch. Base `706ec84ff2` has the same C# source as measured baseline `9a563e814f`; intervening changes are website-only. Twenty-three focused tests, semantic verification and .NET 8 Release compilation passed.

### HTTP revalidation

Fresh Release .NET 10.0.12 ARM64 comparisons use the original frozen baseline `9a563e814f`, default server/concurrent GC, four logical CPUs assigned to the gateway, 200 requests/s and 64 VUs. Each workload uses five fresh gateways in baseline/candidate/baseline/candidate/baseline order, each with 60 s warmup and 60 s measured traffic. One unchanged source process per workload provides the same fixed 4 ms delay. No profiler ran; identical one-second state/process observations remained enabled.

The fresh candidate overlays only the retained measured Execution DLL/PDB on the frozen baseline host. The older HTTP candidate was a whole-project rebuild with additional assembly identity changes; those old outputs are preserved, but are not the isolation evidence for this comparison.

All correctness, actual module/runtime, headroom, completion and error/drop checks passed. Native latency/completed/success counts agree with actual completions in every phase. CPU is the full-phase runtime CPU delta per completed request; independent matching-window OS/runtime checks validate the counter without supplying full-phase performance error bars.

**256 variables / 128 aliases**

| Run | CPU ms/request | CPU C/B, both surrounding controls | p95 ms | p99 ms | p99.9 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1-baseline | 1.472257 | - | 12.321 | 14.835 | 19.621 |
| 2-candidate | 1.427185 | 0.9617–0.9694 | 12.107 | 14.330 | 17.560 |
| 3-baseline | 1.484072 | - | 12.721 | 15.243 | 22.082 |
| 4-candidate | 1.512108 | 1.0130–1.0189 | 12.752 | 14.913 | 19.130 |
| 5-baseline | 1.492687 | - | 12.896 | 15.357 | 20.563 |

**8 variables / 4 aliases**

| Run | CPU ms/request | CPU C/B, both surrounding controls | p95 ms | p99 ms | p99.9 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1-baseline | 0.865858 | - | 10.058 | 12.297 | 18.629 |
| 2-candidate | 0.858847 | 0.9919–1.0101 | 10.224 | 12.422 | 24.239 |
| 3-baseline | 0.850249 | - | 10.135 | 12.365 | 17.565 |
| 4-candidate | 0.871686 | 1.0038–1.0252 | 10.306 | 12.683 | 19.986 |
| 5-baseline | 0.868377 | - | 10.248 | 12.373 | 17.187 |

The large-workload CPU results are mixed, and both candidates have lower p99/p99.9 than both nearby controls. In the ordinary workload, both candidates have higher p95, p99 and p99.9 than both nearby controls. The p99.9 neighboring ranks are also above the baseline neighborhoods, with multiple slow requests clustered in each candidate process. Five-second ranges overlap; requests and blocks are dependent, so these observations do not establish an exact causal effect or statistical equivalence.

[Ordinary HTTP results and lossless raw data](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/d51960ec766abbdc1b855295d09dfb9f72c57d16/docs/perf/fusion-fresh-scaling-20261017/FINAL-HTTP-CAPACITY-8.md), [256-variable HTTP results](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/4198f1dec7f8f9d4cd5dc6cf8d921208a7f0502e/docs/perf/fusion-fresh-scaling-20261017/FINAL-HTTP-CAPACITY-256.md), [independent combined review](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/1405c907137a514e167c6d1df1180f030b4cfa29/docs/perf/fresh-cpu-20261017/http-regression-revalidation/CAPACITY-FINAL-REVIEW.md), [microbenchmark evidence](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/1c99187cfaa6519c80492eb25a1fa2ff1529baa2/docs/perf/fusion-fresh-scaling-20261017/MICRO-V2.md).

### Verdict

**Abandoned because repeated ordinary-workload tail increases leave overall performance benefit unproven.** Both ordinary candidate runs increased p99 and p99.9 against both nearby baselines. CPU was mixed, and the earlier large-workload CPU regression did not repeat; this closure does not claim a generic CPU regression. The repeated ordinary tail signal remains unresolved, so the PR is closed without another benchmark retry.

Fully supplied 8/32/256-variable cases save 808/1,344/21,784 scoped B per call. Sparse input with extra or duplicate used keys instead adds 1,496 B at 32 definitions, with an unmeasured similar reservation risk for first-default-plus-extras. These allocation savings and the passing larger workload do not waive the ordinary HTTP result. No general CPU, latency, RSS, throughput or exact default HTTP byte improvement is claimed. This implementation remains an alternative to #10558; that older PR is unchanged.
